newsitem.title: USA: Missouri row crops show minor improvements in week.
newsitem.headline: Missouri row crops show minor improvements in week.

text.p: The following is the weekly crop summary from the Missouri Agricultural Statistics Service for the week ended Sunday, August 17. --

Rainfall across most of the State has increased topsoil moisture supplies at a critical time for row crops, especially soybeans. However, some northern counties are still in need of more rain for normal crop development.

Condition of the crops for the State as a whole showed only minor improvements from a week earlier, but the benefits from recent showers had not yet been realized at the time of reporting. An average of 4.7 days were suitable for fieldwork during the week of Saturday, August 9th through Friday, August 15th.

The topsoil moisture supply before the effect of additional weekend rain was rated as 16 percent very short, 45 percent short, 37 percent adequate, and 2 percent surplus, a significant improvement from the previous week.
Pasture and range condition is rated as 12 percent very poor, 32 percent poor, 41 percent fair and 15 percent good, a moderate improvement from a week ago.

Ninety-two percent of all soybeans are blooming or beyond and sixty-eight percent of the crop has begun setting pods. Development is about 6 days ahead of both last year and the 5-year average by this date. Development is most advanced in the northwestern and north-central districts with 87 and 78 percent podding respectively, while the least advanced of the main producing areas include the east-cenrtral, southwestern and southeastern districts at about 50 percent podding. Soybean condition is rated as 6 percent very poor, 20 percent poor, 40 percent fair, 30 percent good, and 4 percent excellent, similar to a week ago.

Ninety-one percent of the corn crop is doughing or beyond, forty-eight percent has reached the dent stage, and 6 percent is mature. Denting is about 1 day ahead of last year and 6 days ahead of the 5-year average of 36 percent.

Corn is most advanced in the Bootheel, where 22 percent has reached the mature stage. Corn condition for the State is rated as 9 percent very poor, 21 percent poor, 38 percent fair, 27 percent good and 5 percent excellent, similar to the previous week.

Ninety-two percent of the grain sorghum crop is heading or beyond and twenty-eight percent of the crop is coloring. Heading is 1 week ahead of last year and about 11 days ahead of the 5-year average for this date. Heading is nearly 90 percent or more complete in all districts, except for the east-central with 69 percent. Coloring is most advanced in the Bootheel with 47 percent, followed by the north-central and northwestern districts at 34 and 29 percent respectively. Grain sorghum condition is rated as 7 percent very poor, 17 percent poor, 39 percent fair, 33 percent good and 4 percent excellent, nearly no change from a week ago.

Nine percent of the cotton crop has begun opening bolls, 1 day ahead of last year and 9 days ahead of the 5-year average of 3 percent by this date. Cotton condition is rated as 10 percent very poor, 17 percent poor, 29 percent fair and 42 percent good and 2 percent excellent, a decline from a week ago. Sixty-three percent of the third crop of alfalfa has been cut, compared to 51 percent a year ago and 45 percent normally.

Average temperatures during the past week ranged from 3 degrees below normal in Saint Joseph and Columbia to 2 degrees above normal in Kirksville. Precipitation for the week averaged 2.43 inches. The northwestern and north-central districts recieved the least average rainfall at 1.52 and 1.69 inches, while all other districts received over 2.0 inches, with the southwestern district indicating the heaviest amount at 3.72 inches. The National Weather Service in St. Louis and the USDA-FSA County Offices provided weather summary data.
